hypothesis: A native C++ exact-cover implementation with compact 64-bit difference masks, a larger deduplicated Golomb catalogue, and adaptive rare-compatible-difference branching can reach a complete scope-111 DTS assignment that the prior Python catalogue search did not reach within its node budget.
rationale: The prior global catalogue was a valid new family but its Python DFS reached only depth 4 at 2,000,000 nodes, while the direct CP-SAT and SAT formulations returned UNKNOWN. The mathematical decomposition is exact set packing of seven 15-difference Golomb rulers into 1..111 with six gaps. Native bit masks remove Python loop and memory overhead and allow a materially larger bounded catalogue and search tree without changing the DTS validator or target.
expected_information_gain: Separates Python search overhead from scarcity of compatible scope-111 rows. A validator-accepted assignment would be target progress; substantially greater exact-cover depth without a witness would quantify the remaining combinatorial barrier under a high-throughput implementation.
method: Compile research_tools/search_dts_cpp_exact_cover.cpp under the pinned WSL2 Linux compiler. Generate up to 1,000,000 deduplicated valid scope<=111 Golomb-ruler difference masks from seeded uniform sampling. Build an inverted difference index and perform reversible DFS over seven disjoint rows, choosing the uncovered difference with the fewest currently compatible rows, allowing at most six explicitly skipped differences. Rank compatible rows by inverse difference frequency. Preserve the full raw result and independently validate any complete rows with the repository integer verifier; do not infer infeasibility from a finite catalogue or timeout.
metric: catalog size, exact-cover nodes, maximum depth, gap count, returned rows, and independent DTS validity
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A complete seven-row assignment accepted by the independent integer verifier is exactly a true-objective scope<=111 witness. Catalog/search depth and failure are finite implementation evidence only.

configuration.row_generator: seeded uniform sorted 5-mark samples with internal Golomb check
configuration.branching: rarest currently compatible uncovered difference plus six-gap budget

compute_budget.memory_intent: compact row masks and inverted indexes; bounded one-million-row catalogue

kill_condition: Stop at the first complete assignment, at 360 seconds, at 100,000,000 search nodes, or at a precise runtime failure. Independently validate any returned assignment; do not call a timeout or finite-catalogue failure mathematical infeasibility.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement only if complete rows pass the independent integer verifier

previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: native exact-cover throughput should test a larger finite search without changing the feasible set

interpretation: Pending execution; no result is interpreted before the native exact-cover run and independent verifier.
what_was_learned: Pending execution; the experiment tests whether the prior depth ceiling was implementation throughput rather than compatible-row scarcity.
recommended_next_action: After execution, independently validate any complete rows; otherwise record depth and close or redesign the exact-cover family based on the observed bottleneck.
repetition_justification: This is not a repeat of the prior Python random catalogue: it changes the execution representation to native compact bitsets, increases catalogue and node budgets by orders of magnitude, and uses adaptive compatibility counts and inverse-frequency branching.
